newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FRANCHISEE CENTRAL EUROPEAN FOODS> SAYS PLANS IPO.
newsitem.headline: FRANCHISEE CENTRAL EUROPEAN FOODS> SAYS PLANS IPO.

text.p: The closely-held fast food franchiser Central European Foods Inc.>said on Wednesday it plans to make an initial public offering of stock on a U.S. equities market sometime in the next 12 to 18 months.

Speaking in central Prague at the opening of the world's largest Dunkin' Donuts outlet chief executive Anna K. Hejka-Arczynska said her White Plains, New York-based company would most likely seek listing for its shares on NASDAQ.
"We are looking for a listing on an American stock exchange, probably NASDAQ," she told a news conference.
The company, founded in 1994, has the exclusive licence from Britain's Allied Domecq plc to operate Dunkin' Donuts and Baskin Robbins ice cream franchises in the Czech Republic, Poland, and Slovakia.
Central European Food chairman Witold Peter Michna told Reuters the stock offering was planned for within one year to 18 months, but the size of the issue was still under consideration.

He said the firm, which opened two stores in Warsaw in June, planned 200 outlets by the turn of the century throughout the region with annual turnover estimated at about $80 million and a total workforce of 3,500 employees.
The Czech outlet -- measuring 500 square metres in Prague's central Wenceslas Square -- is the company's first of 30 total Dunkin' Donuts and Baskin-Robbins stores planned for the country.
